name: Korean War
outcome: Armistice — Korean Peninsula divided at 38th parallel; technically no peace treaty signed
short_description: A war between North and South Korea in which a UN force led by the United States fought for the South, and China fought for the North following a North Korean invasion. It ended in an armistice that established the Korean Demilitarized Zone.

sub_events.name: Battle of Pusan Perimeter
sub_events.short_description: UN forces held a desperate defensive perimeter around the port of Pusan against overwhelming North Korean forces.

sub_events.name: Battle of Inchon
sub_events.short_description: A daring UN amphibious assault behind enemy lines that turned the tide of the war.

sub_events.name: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
sub_events.short_description: UN forces were encircled by Chinese troops in freezing conditions; a brutal fighting withdrawal became legendary.

name: First Indochina War
outcome: French defeat; Geneva Accords divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel
short_description: A war between France and the Việt Minh independence movement, culminating in the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu and the partition of Vietnam.

sub_events.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
sub_events.short_description: The decisive battle in which Việt Minh forces surrounded and destroyed the French garrison, ending the war.

name: Algerian War of Independence
outcome: Algerian independence; over 1 million Europeans left Algeria
short_description: A brutal independence war fought between Algerian nationalist guerrillas (FLN) and France, marked by widespread torture, terrorism, and civilian massacres on both sides.

sub_events.name: Battle of Algiers
sub_events.short_description: A brutal urban guerrilla campaign by the FLN, met with systematic torture and repression by French paratroopers.

name: Vietnam War
outcome: North Vietnamese victory; reunification of Vietnam under communist rule
short_description: A prolonged Cold War-era conflict in which North Vietnam and its Viet Cong allies fought to reunify Vietnam under communism, opposed by South Vietnam and the United States. It ended with the fall of Saigon.

sub_events.name: Tet Offensive
sub_events.short_description: A massive coordinated surprise attack by North Vietnamese forces during Tết, which shifted American public opinion against the war.

sub_events.name: Battle of Huế
sub_events.short_description: One of the bloodiest and longest battles of the war, fought house-to-house through Huế's ancient citadel.

name: Six-Day War
outcome: Decisive Israeli victory; Israel captured the Sinai Peninsula, Gaza Strip, West Bank, and Golan Heights
short_description: A swift and decisive war in which Israel launched preemptive strikes against Arab coalition forces, tripling its territory in six days. The occupation of Palestinian territories continues to shape the Middle East conflict today.

sub_events.name: Operation Focus
sub_events.short_description: Israel's devastating preemptive air strike that destroyed the Arab air forces on the ground within hours.

name: Yom Kippur War
outcome: Military stalemate; led to the Camp David Accords and Egyptian-Israeli peace treaty
short_description: Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel during Yom Kippur, initially overrunning Israeli positions. Israel counterattacked successfully, eventually crossing the Suez Canal. The war led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

name: Soviet-Afghan War
outcome: Soviet withdrawal; Afghan civil war continued; rise of the Taliban
short_description: The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan to support its communist government against Mujahideen guerrillas backed by the US, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The decade-long war devastated Afghanistan and contributed to the collapse of the USSR.

sub_events.name: Operation Cyclone
sub_events.short_description: The CIA's programme to arm and finance Mujahideen fighters — one of the longest and most expensive covert operations in CIA history.

name: Iran–Iraq War
outcome: Stalemate; UN-brokered ceasefire with no territorial changes; estimated 500,000–1,000,000 dead
short_description: One of the 20th century's bloodiest wars, fought between Iraq under Saddam Hussein and Iran under Ayatollah Khomeini. Notable for the use of chemical weapons by Iraq and human wave infantry assaults by Iran. Ended in a stalemate.

name: Falklands War
outcome: British victory; Argentine surrender; islands remain under British control
short_description: Argentina invaded the British-held Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas). Britain dispatched a naval task force 8,000 miles to retake them. Argentina surrendered after 74 days. The war led to the fall of Argentina's military junta.

sub_events.name: Sinking of the General Belgrano
sub_events.short_description: A British submarine torpedoed the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano, killing 323 sailors — the most controversial action of the war.

name: Gulf War
outcome: Coalition victory; Iraq expelled from Kuwait; but Saddam Hussein remained in power
short_description: Iraq under Saddam Hussein invaded Kuwait, triggering a massive UN-sanctioned coalition military response led by the US. Operation Desert Storm's air and ground campaign liberated Kuwait in 100 hours of ground combat.

sub_events.name: Operation Desert Storm
sub_events.short_description: The US-led coalition's air and ground offensive that liberated Kuwait in just 42 days, featuring devastating air bombardment followed by 100 hours of ground combat.

name: Rwandan Genocide
outcome: RPF military victory; an estimated 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu killed in 100 days
short_description: In 100 days, Hutu extremists systematically murdered an estimated 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu in Rwanda — one of the fastest genocides in history. The international community failed to intervene. The RPF eventually halted the killings.

name: First Chechen War
outcome: Russian withdrawal; Chechen de facto independence (Khasavyurt Accord)
short_description: Russia launched a military campaign to prevent Chechen independence, resulting in urban warfare and heavy civilian casualties, particularly in Grozny. Russia withdrew after suffering humiliating defeats.

sub_events.name: Battle of Grozny (1994–1995)
sub_events.short_description: Russian forces attempted to storm Grozny on New Year's Eve 1994 and were devastated in fierce urban fighting. The city was eventually captured at enormous cost.

name: Bosnian War
outcome: Dayton Agreement; Bosnia divided into two entities; Republika Srpska and Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
short_description: Following Yugoslavia's breakup, Bosnia's declaration of independence triggered war between Bosniak, Serbian, and Croatian factions. Marked by ethnic cleansing, mass rape as a weapon of war, and the Srebrenica massacre.

sub_events.name: Srebrenica Massacre
sub_events.short_description: Bosnian Serb forces murdered over 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys — Europe's worst mass killing since WWII, ruled a genocide by the International Court of Justice.

sub_events.name: Siege of Sarajevo
sub_events.short_description: The longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare history, lasting 1,425 days. Serbian forces sniped civilians and shelled the city daily.

name: Kosovo War
outcome: NATO victory; Yugoslav forces withdrew; Kosovo under UN administration; declared independence in 2008
short_description: Serbian forces conducted ethnic cleansing against Kosovo Albanians, triggering a NATO air campaign (Operation Allied Force). Over 1 million Albanians were displaced. Kosovo eventually declared independence in 2008.

sub_events.name: Operation Allied Force
sub_events.short_description: NATO's 78-day air campaign against Yugoslavia — the first NATO combat operation in history, conducted without UN Security Council authorization.

name: Second Chechen War
outcome: Russian victory; Chechnya integrated back into Russia under Kadyrov
short_description: Russia relaunched its military campaign in Chechnya following apartment bombings in Russia and a Chechen incursion into Dagestan. Grozny was razed. Russia installed Akhmad Kadyrov's government, ending the separatist conflict.

name: War in Afghanistan
outcome: Taliban returned to power; US and NATO forces withdrew after 20 years; longest war in US history
short_description: Launched after the September 11 attacks, the US-led invasion toppled the Taliban government and killed Al-Qaeda leaders. Two decades of nation-building failed; the Taliban retook Kabul in August 2021 as US forces withdrew.

sub_events.name: Battle of Tora Bora
sub_events.short_description: US and Afghan forces attempted to capture Osama bin Laden in mountain cave complexes. He escaped into Pakistan.

sub_events.name: Fall of Kabul (2021)
sub_events.short_description: The Taliban swept into Kabul as the Afghan government collapsed, ending 20 years of US-backed rule in a matter of days.

name: Iraq War
outcome: Saddam Hussein overthrown and executed; prolonged insurgency; sectarian civil war; ISIS emerged
short_description: The US-led invasion toppled Saddam Hussein's regime based on claims of WMDs that proved false. The resulting power vacuum triggered a brutal insurgency, sectarian civil war, and the emergence of ISIS.

sub_events.name: Battle of Fallujah
sub_events.short_description: The bloodiest battle of the Iraq War — US Marines fought house-to-house through Fallujah in one of the most intense urban battles since WWII.

name: Darfur Conflict
outcome: Ongoing; ICC issued arrest warrant for Omar al-Bashir for genocide
short_description: The Sudanese government and Arab Janjaweed militias systematically attacked non-Arab African populations in Darfur, killing hundreds of thousands and displacing millions. The ICC ruled it genocide. Conflict continues in various forms.

name: 2006 Lebanon War
outcome: Ceasefire; Hezbollah survived and claimed victory; Israel failed to achieve strategic goals
short_description: Triggered by Hezbollah's cross-border raid and capture of Israeli soldiers, Israel launched an air campaign and ground invasion of Lebanon. Hezbollah's survival was seen as a strategic defeat for Israel.

name: Libyan Civil War
outcome: Gaddafi killed (2011); country split between rival governments; ongoing fragmented conflict
short_description: Arab Spring protests escalated into civil war; NATO airstrikes helped rebels overthrow Muammar Gaddafi. Post-Gaddafi Libya fragmented into rival factions and militia rule, becoming a failed state and migration crisis hub.

name: Syrian Civil War
outcome: Assad retained power over most territory; rebel strongholds remain; millions displaced; ISIS defeated territorially
short_description: Syria's Arab Spring protests triggered a civil war drawing in Russia, Iran, Turkey, the US, and ISIS. One of the world's worst humanitarian disasters — half of Syria's population displaced, 500,000+ dead.

sub_events.name: Battle of Aleppo
sub_events.short_description: A four-year siege of Syria's second city. Russian-backed Assad forces recaptured the rebel-held east of Aleppo in brutal fighting.

sub_events.name: Battle of Raqqa
sub_events.short_description: US-backed Kurdish-led SDF forces fought ISIS for four months to liberate the Islamic State's self-declared capital.

name: War in Donbas
outcome: Frozen conflict; superseded by Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022
short_description: Following Russia's annexation of Crimea, Russian-backed separatists seized parts of eastern Ukraine. Eight years of trench warfare and ceasefire violations followed, ended by Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

name: Russia–Ukraine War
outcome: Ongoing — Russia controls approximately 20% of Ukrainian territory
short_description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022 — the largest conventional war in Europe since WWII. Ukraine mounted fierce resistance with Western support. The conflict has caused mass civilian casualties and a global humanitarian crisis.

sub_events.name: Battle of Kyiv
sub_events.short_description: Russia's initial assault to capture Kyiv was repelled by Ukrainian defenders in 33 days. Russian forces withdrew from around the capital.

sub_events.name: Siege of Mariupol
sub_events.short_description: Russian forces besieged and bombarded Mariupol for 86 days. Ukrainian defenders including Azov Battalion held out in the Azovstal steel plant before surrendering.

name: Yemeni Civil War
outcome: Ongoing — UN calls it world's worst humanitarian crisis
short_description: Houthi rebels seized Yemen's capital Sanaa, triggering a Saudi-led military coalition intervention. The war has caused the world's worst humanitarian crisis, with millions facing famine and cholera epidemics.

name: Rise and Fall of ISIS
outcome: ISIS territorial caliphate destroyed; ISIS continues as insurgency
short_description: ISIS declared a caliphate across Iraq and Syria in 2014, controlling territory the size of the UK. A global coalition of enemies gradually destroyed the caliphate by 2019, though ISIS continues as a decentralized terrorist network.

sub_events.name: Battle of Mosul
sub_events.short_description: A 9-month battle to retake Iraq's second-largest city from ISIS — one of the largest urban battles since WWII.

name: Tigray War
outcome: Pretoria Agreement ceasefire; TPLF disarms; humanitarian crisis ongoing
short_description: One of the deadliest conflicts of the 21st century. Ethiopian and Eritrean forces fought the TPLF in Tigray, with atrocities committed by all sides. Famine and mass atrocities affected millions.

name: Sudan Civil War (2023–present)
outcome: Ongoing — largest displacement crisis in the world as of 2024
short_description: War erupted between Sudan's army (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), creating the world's largest displacement crisis — over 10 million people forced from their homes. Mass atrocities reported in Darfur.

name: Suez Crisis
outcome: Egyptian political victory; British and French withdrawal; UN peacekeepers deployed
short_description: An invasion of Egypt by Israel, followed by the UK and France, aimed at regaining Western control of the Suez Canal and removing Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser.

sub_events.name: Operation Musketeer
sub_events.short_description: Anglo-French airborne and amphibious landings at Port Said.

name: Lebanese Civil War
outcome: Taif Agreement; Syrian occupation of Lebanon until 2005; disbandment of most militias
short_description: A complex multi-faceted civil war in Lebanon resulting from sectarian tensions, PLO presence, and regional interventions by Syria and Israel.

sub_events.name: 1982 Israeli Invasion of Lebanon
sub_events.short_description: Israel invaded Lebanon to expel the PLO, leading to the Siege of Beirut.

name: 2023 Israel–Hamas War
outcome: Ongoing major conflict; heavy destruction of Gaza infrastructure; widespread humanitarian crisis
short_description: A major conflict triggered by Hamas attacks on October 7, 2023, followed by a massive Israeli military campaign in the Gaza Strip and regional flare-ups.

sub_events.name: October 7 Hamas Assault
sub_events.short_description: Surprise cross-border assault by Hamas militants.

name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
outcome: Revolution crushed by Soviet invasion; pro-Soviet government re-established under János Kádár
short_description: A nationwide revolution against the Soviet-imposed government of Hungary, brutally crushed by Soviet tanks and troops.

name: The Troubles
outcome: Good Friday Agreement (1998); power-sharing executive created; demilitarization
short_description: An ethno-nationalist conflict in Northern Ireland lasting three decades over the constitutional status of Northern Ireland.

sub_events.name: Bloody Sunday
sub_events.short_description: British soldiers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a civil rights protest rally.

name: Transnistria War
outcome: Ceasefire; Transnistria established as an unrecognised de facto break-away state backed by Russian forces
short_description: A short war following the dissolution of the Soviet Union between Moldovan forces and Transnistrian separatists supported by Russia.

name: Russo-Georgian War
outcome: Russian military victory; Russia officially recognized South Ossetia and Abkhazia
short_description: A brief war between Georgia, Russia, and the Russian-backed self-proclaimed republics of South Ossetia and Abkhazia.

sub_events.name: Battle of Tskhinvali
sub_events.short_description: Georgian assault followed by overwhelming Russian armored counter-attack.

name: Sino-Indian War
outcome: Chinese victory; unilateral Chinese ceasefire and retreat to Line of Actual Control (LAC)
short_description: A high-altitude mountain conflict between China and India over disputed Himalayan borders in Aksai Chin and Arunachal Pradesh.

name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
outcome: UN-mandated ceasefire; Tashkent Declaration restored pre-war status quo
short_description: A five-week war that began following Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar, which was designed to infiltrate forces into Jammu and Kashmir.

name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971
outcome: Decisive Indian victory; Instrument of Surrender signed in Dhaka; Independence of Bangladesh
short_description: A major conflict triggered by the genocide in East Pakistan, ending in Indian victory and the creation of Bangladesh.

sub_events.name: Surrender at Dhaka
sub_events.short_description: 93,000 Pakistani soldiers surrendered to joint Indian and Mukti Bahini forces.

name: Cambodian Civil War & Khmer Rouge Era
outcome: Khmer Rouge victory in 1975 followed by Cambodian Genocide (~1.5-2M dead); ended by Vietnamese invasion in 1979
short_description: A military conflict that pitted the forces of the Khmer Rouge against the government of Cambodia, leading to the brutal Cambodian Genocide.

sub_events.name: Fall of Phnom Penh
sub_events.short_description: Khmer Rouge entered Phnom Penh and forcibly evacuated the city.

name: Sino-Vietnamese War
outcome: Both sides claimed victory; Chinese withdrawal; border skirmishes continued through the 1980s
short_description: A brief border war launched by China against Vietnam in response to Vietnam's invasion and occupation of Cambodia.

name: Sri Lankan Civil War
outcome: Decisive military victory by Sri Lankan Armed Forces; destruction of LTTE leadership
short_description: A 26-year armed conflict fought by the Tamil Tigers to create an independent Tamil state in the north and east of Sri Lanka.

name: Kargil War
outcome: Indian victory; recapture of all infiltrated posts in Kargil district
short_description: An armed conflict between India and Pakistan in the Kargil district of Kashmir following Pakistani infiltration across the Line of Control.

name: Myanmar Civil War (2021–present)
outcome: Ongoing widespread civil war following 2021 military coup; resistance alliances control significant territory
short_description: A major escalation of Myanmar's long-running internal conflicts following the February 2021 military coup that ousted Aung San Suu Kyi.

sub_events.name: Operation 1027
sub_events.short_description: Three Brotherhood Alliance offensive capturing major border towns and military outposts.

name: Congo Crisis
outcome: Re-unification of Congo; assassination of Patrice Lumumba; Mobutu Sese Seko seized power
short_description: A period of political upheaval and conflict in the Republic of the Congo immediately following independence from Belgium.

name: Nigerian Civil War
outcome: Nigerian victory; surrender of Biafran forces; re-absorption of Biafra into Nigeria
short_description: A brutal civil war caused by the secession of the Eastern Region of Nigeria as the self-proclaimed Republic of Biafra.

name: Angolan Civil War
outcome: MPLA military victory following death of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi; UNITA converted to political party
short_description: A major 27-year Cold War proxy civil war in Angola that erupted immediately after independence from Portugal.

sub_events.name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
sub_events.short_description: The largest conventional battle on the African continent since WWII.

name: Ogaden War
outcome: Ethiopian victory; complete Somali withdrawal from Ogaden region
short_description: A military conflict fought between Somalia and Ethiopia over the disputed Ogaden region.

name: First Congo War
outcome: AFDL victory; overthrow of Mobutu Sese Seko; Zaire renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo
short_description: A foreign-assisted civil war in Zaire that deposed long-time dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.

name: Second Congo War
outcome: Sun City Agreement; Transitional Government of DR Congo established; deadly ongoing eastern DRC insurgency
short_description: The deadliest conflict worldwide since World War II, involving nine African nations and over 20 armed groups.

sub_events.name: Siege of Kinshasa
sub_events.short_description: Angolan and Zimbabwean military intervention saved Kinshasa from falling to Rwandan-backed rebels.

name: Sierra Leone Civil War
outcome: Government victory; disarming of RUF; UN deployment and Special Court for Sierra Leone established
short_description: A brutal civil war driven by diamond mining ("blood diamonds") notorious for atrocities and child soldiers.

name: Cuban Revolution

side_b: 26th of July Movement (Fidel Castro, Che Guevara)

outcome: Overthrow of Fulgencio Batista; establishment of socialist state under Fidel Castro
short_description: An armed revolt conducted by Fidel Castro's 26th of July Movement against the military dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista.

name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
outcome: Decisive Cuban victory; failure of CIA invasion plan; consolidation of Castro's power
short_description: A failed landing operation on the southwestern coast of Cuba by a CIA-sponsored paramilitary group of Cuban exiles.

name: Guatemalan Civil War
outcome: Peace Accords of 1996; UN Truth Commission documented state genocide against Mayan populations
short_description: A 36-year civil war fought between the government of Guatemala and leftist rebel groups, marked by state genocide against Indigenous Mayans.

name: Football War
outcome: OAS ceasefire; Salvadoran troop withdrawal
short_description: A brief four-day war between El Salvador and Honduras, triggered by land reform disputes and escalated during 1970 World Cup qualifiers.

name: Nicaraguan Revolution & Contra War
outcome: Sandinistas overthrew Somoza in 1979; Contra war ended with 1990 democratic elections and demobilization
short_description: The overthrow of the Somoza dictatorship by the Sandinistas, followed by a US-backed insurgency by the Contras.

name: Salvadoran Civil War
outcome: Chapultepec Peace Accords (1992); military reformed; FMLN legalized as political party
short_description: A 12-year conflict between the military-led government of El Salvador and a coalition of guerrilla groups known as the FMLN.

name: Colombian Conflict
outcome: 2016 Havana Peace Accord disarmed main FARC body; ongoing fighting with ELN and FARC dissidents
short_description: A low-intensity asymmetric war between the Colombian government, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and leftist guerrillas.

name: Nagorno-Karabakh Conflicts
outcome: 2023 Azerbaijani military offensive resulted in complete collapse of Artsakh and dissolution of the break-away republic
short_description: An ethnic and territorial conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan over the Nagorno-Karabakh region.

sub_events.name: 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh War
sub_events.short_description: 44-day war in which Azerbaijani forces reclaimed surrounding territories using modern drone warfare.

name: Tajikistani Civil War
outcome: 1997 General Peace Agreement; Emomali Rahmon established centralized rule; opposition integrated into government
short_description: A civil war fought in Tajikistan following independence from the Soviet Union between regional clans and Islamist opposition.

name: World War II
outcome: Allied victory; unconditional surrender of Axis powers; creation of the United Nations; advent of atomic age; start of Cold War
short_description: The global military conflict that involved the vast majority of the world's nations forming two opposing military alliances: the Allies and the Axis.

sub_events.name: Invasion of Poland
sub_events.short_description: German blitzkrieg attack triggering the outbreak of World War II in Europe.

sub_events.name: Battle of Stalingrad
sub_events.short_description: Bloodiest battle in human history (~2M casualties); turning point on the Eastern Front.

sub_events.name: Normandy Landings (D-Day)
sub_events.short_description: Operation Overlord: massive Allied amphibious invasion establishing the Western Front.

sub_events.name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
sub_events.short_description: United States dropped atomic bombs, precipitating Japan's unconditional surrender.

name: World War I
outcome: Allied victory; Armistice of 11 November 1918; Treaty of Versailles; collapse of German, Russian, Austro-Hungarian, and Ottoman empires
short_description: A global conflict centered in Europe that mobilized over 70 million military personnel and reshaped world geopolitics.

sub_events.name: Battle of the Somme
sub_events.short_description: One of the bloodiest military battles in history with over 1 million casualties.

sub_events.name: Battle of Verdun
sub_events.short_description: Longest battle of WWI; brutal attrition between French and German armies.

sub_events.name: Gallipoli Campaign
sub_events.short_description: Allied naval and land campaign intended to knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war.

name: Second Sino-Japanese War
alternate_names: War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
outcome: Chinese victory following Allied defeat of Japan in WWII; Taiwan returned to China; preceded resumed Chinese Civil War
short_description: A massive military conflict fought primarily between the Republic of China and the Empire of Japan, merging into World War II.

sub_events.name: Nanking Massacre
sub_events.short_description: Mass murder and mass rape committed by Japanese troops against Nanking residents.

name: Chinese Civil War
outcome: CCP victory; Proclamation of the People's Republic of China; KMT retreat to Taiwan
short_description: A long civil war between the Nationalist government of Kuomintang and the Chinese Communist Party, fundamentally transforming Asia.

sub_events.name: The Long March
sub_events.short_description: A historic 6,000-mile military retreat undertaken by the Red Army of the CCP.

name: Russian Civil War

side_b: Allied Intervention Forces (UK, US, France, Japan)

outcome: Bolshevik victory; creation of the Soviet Union (USSR)
short_description: A complex multi-party civil war in the former Russian Empire following the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution.

name: Spanish Civil War
outcome: Nationalist victory; establishment of Francoist dictatorship (1939–1975)
short_description: A major conflict between Spanish Republicans and Nationalists led by General Francisco Franco, serving as a proving ground for WWII tactics.

sub_events.name: Bombing of Guernica
sub_events.short_description: Aerial bombing of Basque town by Nazi Condor Legion, immortalized by Picasso.

name: Mexican Revolution
outcome: Overthrow of Porfirio Díaz; adoption of 1917 Constitution of Mexico; creation of modern Mexican state
short_description: A major armed struggle that transformed Mexican culture and government, dismantling the Porfiriato regime.

name: Russo-Japanese War
outcome: Japanese victory; Treaty of Portsmouth; Japan recognized as an Asian world power; Russian Revolution of 1905 triggered
short_description: The first modern war in which an Asian power defeated a major European imperial power, fought over Korea and Manchuria.

sub_events.name: Battle of Tsushima
sub_events.short_description: Decisive naval battle in which the Japanese fleet destroyed two-thirds of the Russian Baltic Fleet.

name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
outcome: Israeli victory; 1949 Armistice Agreements; Green Line established; Palestinian displacement (Nakba)
short_description: The first war in the Arab-Israeli conflict, fought immediately following the Israeli Declaration of Independence.

name: Indonesian National Revolution
outcome: Dutch recognition of Indonesian independence at the Dutch-Indonesian Round Table Conference
short_description: An armed conflict and diplomatic struggle between Indonesia and the Netherlands following Indonesia's declaration of independence.

name: Balkan Wars
outcome: Ottoman Empire lost almost all European territories; tensions directly set the stage for World War I
short_description: Two military conflicts in southeastern Europe that stripped the Ottoman Empire of its European holdings.

name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
outcome: Italian annexation of Ethiopia; formation of Italian East Africa; exposed complete weakness of the League of Nations
short_description: An imperialist war of aggression launched by Fascist Italy under Mussolini against Ethiopia.

name: Winter War
outcome: Moscow Peace Treaty; Finland ceded 9% of its territory but retained national independence
short_description: A Soviet invasion of Finland three months after the outbreak of World War II, famous for fierce Finnish winter defense.

name: Greek Civil War
outcome: Government victory; Greece joined NATO; early battleground of the Truman Doctrine
short_description: A civil war in Greece between government forces backed by Britain/US and communist insurgents backed by Yugoslavia.

name: Chaco War
outcome: Paraguayan victory; Treaty of Buenos Aires granted Paraguay three-quarters of the disputed Gran Chaco region
short_description: The bloodiest interstate war in South America during the 20th century, fought between Bolivia and Paraguay over Gran Chaco.

name: Philippine-American War
outcome: US victory; annexation of the Philippines as a US territory until 1946
short_description: An armed conflict between the First Philippine Republic and the United States following the Spanish-American War.

name: Second Boer War
outcome: British victory; Treaty of Vereeniging annexed Boer Republics into the British Empire
short_description: A war fought between the British Empire and two independent Boer republics over empire control in South Africa.
